mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower financing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 or negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 3.5% in a single month, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 3.5), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (FEDFUNDS increase and UNRATE decrease) fails to produce negative returns in more than 40% of instances, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a sustained decline in the unemployment rate signals tight labor markets that boost corporate profits and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation rate, as measured by the monthly change in PAYEMS, indicates strengthening economic conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1200 thousand units in a month, it signals robust consumer demand for housing and related sectors, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate sustained economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered instances (HOUST > 1200.0), or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong economic activity across multiple sectors, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in INDPRO and HOUST fails to produce positive returns in more than 40% of instances, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 110.0), a slowdown in manufacturing output growth signals potential supply chain disruptions that increase inflationary pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors price in higher costs.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 110.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
